Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me + intro by.description:
1992 — France-USA — David Lynch — 134 min — Cert 18

The big-screen offshoot of David Lynch’s era-defining TV series is a darker, more nightmarish journey into small-town America.

This feature-length follow-up to the hit TV series has been heralded as a masterpiece in horror. A terrifying fever-dream, it features a stunning performance from Sheryl Lee, recreating the final days of Laura Palmer. David Bowie contributes a short but impactful appearance as Agent Jeffries and, of course, Kyle MacLachlan is back as Agent Dale Cooper, albeit in a slightly scaled-back role. Contains graphic violence, disturbing imagery and scenes of a sexual nature. See other screenings of Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me .

_additional_info.title: Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me

The Voice of Hind Rajab.description:
2025 — Tunisia-France — Kaouther Ben Hania — 89 min

The director of Four Daughters presents the events surrounding the death of a young Palestinian girl.

One January afternoon in 2024, the Palestine Red Crescent Society receives a call. On the other end of the phone is a six-year-old girl, surrounded by dead bodies. Audible gunfire punctuates her pleas for help, as she hides from encroaching Israeli tanks. From their offices 50 miles away, volunteers fight against red-tape and internal tensions to deliver a rescue ambulance, distress mounting as time marches on. Blending documentary and fiction in service of undeniable truth, audio recordings of Hind’s final hours are woven seamlessly into this recreation of the mission to save her. Oscar-nominated filmmaker Kaouther Ben Hania balances hope and helplessness on a tightrope, while honouring both the victims of violence and those who fight to protect them. This is essential filmmaking that cuts through the noise, capturing the human devastation at the heart of war. Ruby McGuigan, Programme Development Manager Contains distressing scenes.

25 and Under: An Introduction to Constru.description:
An introduction to this season, hosted by season curator Xavier Alexandre Pillai.

Multicultural television was a unique moment in TV history, creating a global style of programming that traced so many stories. Season curator Xavier Alexandre Pillai will reflect on his highlights of the movement and discuss the potency of using archive as a tool of reassembly. Free for those aged 16-25 (please book in advance). Don’t forget to book your £4 ticket to Multicultural TV on Channel 4 , which screens following this talk.

_additional_info.title: 25 and Under: An Introduction to Constructed, Told, Spoken

Preview: 100 Nights of Hero + Q&A with w.description:
2025 — UK — Julia Jackman — 90 min

Julia Jackman’s second feature, a hit as the closing night gala at BFI London Film Festival 2025, is a playful fairytale.

A fairytale marriage is not what new bride Cherry is experiencing with avoidant husband Jerome. Unbeknown to her, there’s mischief afoot. It appears in the form of handsome stranger Manfred, whose attentions towards Cherry appear to be more than friendly. It’s up to her devoted maid, Hero, to intervene and hopefully save the day. Adapted from Isabel Greenberg’s graphic novel, Jackman’s charming, witty and devilishly mischievous romp is a refreshing take on love, gender, sexuality and the power of storytelling. Tickets £17, concessions £14 (Members pay £2.50).

Afterimage.description:
2016 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 98 min

The life of Polish avant-garde artists becomes an inspiration for Andrzej Wajda’s explorations of resilience in the face of oppression.

In his final film, Wajda returns to previously explored themes of personal and artistic resistance to an authoritarian state and ideology. Based on the life of avant-garde painter and theorist Władysław Strzemiński, the film chronicles his struggles against expulsion from state institutions, and erasure from a nation’s collective memory, as a result of political and artistic convictions that were at odds with the official Stalinist post-war doctrine. Poland 1955. Director Andrzej Wajda. 13min. Digital (restoration). With English subtitles A lyrical documentary about a respected Polish sculptor Xawery Dunikowski.

The War Trilogy: A Generation.description:
1954 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 87 min

Andrzej Wajda’s feature directorial debut is a portrait of Polish underground fighters during the Second World War.

Set in 1942, on the outskirts of Nazi-occupied Warsaw, Wajda’s striking feature debut centres on Stach, and a group of young, anti-German underground fighters, as they prepare for a new mission. The film not only established Wajda as a director to watch, it foregrounded key recurring themes in his work – honour, courage and sacrifice – and presents a stark account of the tragedies of conflict. A landmark film and the first in the director’s acclaimed war trilogy, A Generation helped change the trajectory of Polish cinema. Contains a scene of suicide. Poland 1953. Director Andrzej Wajda. 11min. Digital (restoration). With English subtitles This fascinating short captures a bustling city at night and was shot by Jerzy Lipman, the cinematographer on A Generation. Joint ticket available with the screenings of Kanal and Ashes and Diamonds on Sunday 15 February. Tickets £28.50, concessions £22.50 (Members pay £3 less). Book in person at the box office or by phone on 020 7928 3232. Also available on BFI Player

Amores Perros.description:
2000 — Mexico — Alejandro González Iñárritu — 148 min — Cert 18

Three stories of animalistic desire drive this modern Mexican classic, the debut of Alejandro González Iñárritu.

Intertwining three storylines on the theme of animalistic desires, Amores Perros charts the fates of a young man caught up in the world of dogfighting, a supermodel whose career is wrecked by a car accident and a homeless hitman who tries to connect to his estranged daughter. Iñárritu’s brilliant, but often brutal, feature debut contains shocking scenes of dog fighting, all of which was simulated for the camera. Also available on BFI Player

An Introduction to Andrzej Wajda.description:
A richly-illustrated discussion about the work of Polish filmmaker Andrzej Wajda.

Join our invited guests for an exploration of Andrzej Wajda’s work, taking a closer look at the thematic preoccupations emerging from his filmography and the context for his cinema. Considering his best-known titles and spotlighting less-known gems, the speakers will illuminate the trajectory of Wajda’s work, discuss his influential role within Polish film history and reflect on why his films still resonate today. Tickets £6.50. Joint ticket available with The Wedding + intro on Wednesday 11 February 20:40 NFT2 £17, concessions £14 (Members pay £2.50 less). Book in person at the box office or by phone on 020 7928 3232.

Arts and Multiculturalism.description:
We look at the artistic and social spaces created by multicultural communities and documented by multicultural TV.

LWT 1980. Director Nic Phillips. 26min. Digital LWT 1980. Director Nic Phillips. 26min. Digital Channel 4 1989. Directors David Maloney, John O’ Brien. 30min. Digital BBC 1994. Series Producer Yasmin Anwar. 29min. Digital Outside of the traditional structure of national institutions, Black and Asian Britons created unique artistic communities, often taking the form of collectives or commercially minded organisations, which still aimed for access to the mainstream. From Blues Parties to video distribution in Southall, each iteration of new movements existed in parallel to the mainstream, with some breaking through while others plateaued.

The War Trilogy: Ashes and Diamonds.description:
1958 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 100 min

One of Martin Scorsese’s most beloved films, Andrzej Wajda’s piercing drama stars iconic Polish actor Zbigniew Cybulski as a tragic hero in Poland in the aftermath of the Second World War.

In the last days of the Second World War, Maciek, a Polish resistance fighter, is tasked with the assassination of a Communist official. When he meets Krystyna, he is offered a glimpse of a world beyond war and destruction, and questions his assignment. Wajda’s classic drama, which cemented his position as a world-class filmmaker, features an iconic central performance by Cybulski – the ‘Polish James Dean’ – who contributes immeasurably to this probing look at the complex post-war future for a new nation and its people. It’s essential viewing. Joint ticket available with the screenings of A Generation and Kanal on Sunday 15 February. Tickets £28.50, concessions £22.50 (Members pay £3 less). Book in person at the box office or by phone on 020 7928 3232. The KINOTEKA Polish Film Festival Opening screening of Ashes and Diamonds on Wednesday 4 February will include an extended intro. Also available on BFI Player

In the last days of the Second World War, Maciek, a Polish resistance fighter, is tasked with the assassination of a Communist official. When he meets Krystyna, he is offered a glimpse of a world beyond war and destruction, and questions his assignment. Wajda’s classic drama, which cemented his position as a world-class filmmaker, features an iconic central performance by Cybulski – the ‘Polish James Dean’ – who contributes immeasurably to this probing look at the complex post-war future for a new nation and its people. It’s essential viewing. See other screenings of Ashes and Diamonds . Also available on BFI Player

The Ashes + intro by writer Michael Broo.description:
1965 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 227 min

Andrzej Wajda’s huge historical epic, unfolding across a large canvas, is an account of Poland’s participation in the Napoleonic wars.

This epic tale of the Napoleonic wars and Poles’ participation in them provides Wajda with an opportunity to consider thorny questions around heroism and patriotism. A young nobleman partakes in the conflict, fighting for Poland’s freedom while searching for his own self. Wajda worked with a higher budget and on a much larger scale to create this visually dazzling CinemaScope drama, which examines nationhood and national identity. See other screenings of The Ashes .

The Ashes.description:
1965 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 227 min

Andrzej Wajda’s huge historical epic, unfolding across a large canvas, is an account of Poland’s participation in the Napoleonic wars.

The screening of The Ashes on Saturday 28 February will be introduced by writer Michael Brooke.

Assimilationist TV + intro by Sarita Mal.description:
Early multicultural television was initiated by the state to aid integration and provides a fascinating insight into the movement.

BBC 1960. Series Editor Huw Wheldon. 24min. Digital BBC 1969. Series Producer Saleem Shaheed. 23min. Digital. With English subtitles BBC 1970. Series Producer Saleem Shaheed. 21min. Digital. With English subtitles Nai Zindagi Naya Jeevan discusses the political climate and features former Labour politician Merlyn Rees, who affirms the governments support for migrant communities. Assimilationist programming was seen as unnecessary for West Indians. Monitor speaks to West Indian author Edgar Mittelholzer, alongside George Lamming, who offer contrasting views on British culture and Caribbean identity.

Au hasard Balthazar.description:
1966 — France — Robert Bresson — 95 min

A donkey’s journey, being passed between cruel masters, is the basis of Bresson’s heartbreaking masterpiece.

Animal protagonists are traditionally the preserve of sentimental stories for children. Bresson’s tragic masterpiece, about the travails of a donkey, has the simple force of a fable, but it also presents a brutally pessimistic vision of the world. Punished, maltreated, used and only occasionally loved, Balthazar is put to work by one keeper after another, bearing silent witness to the folly and petty cruelties of his human masters. Bresson’s pared down style elicits pathos from this classic tale.

Beauty and the Beast + intro by Disniver.description:
1991 — USA — Gary Trousdale, Kirk Wise — 84 min

Disney’s modern classic tells ‘the tale as old as time’ as Belle goes to live with a beast in an enchanted castle.

Belle is sent to live with a reclusive beast, knowing little about the place and the spell cast across the entire household. As Belle and her erstwhile captor grow closer, her father and the villagers decide to act, which puts everyone in terrible danger. The seamless blend of traditional and CGI animation, particularly in the now-classic ballroom sequence, set a benchmark for what animation could achieve. It became the first full-length animated feature to be nominated for the Best Picture Oscar. See other screenings of Beauty and the Beast .

Beauty and the Beast.description:
1991 — USA — Gary Trousdale, Kirk Wise — 84 min

Disney’s modern classic tells ‘the tale as old as time’ as Belle goes to live with a beast in an enchanted castle.

Belle is sent to live with a reclusive beast, knowing little about the place and the spell cast across the entire household. As Belle and her erstwhile captor grow closer, her father and the villagers decide to act, which puts everyone in terrible danger. It became the first full-length animated feature to be nominated for the Best Picture Oscar. The screening on Saturday 7 March will be presented with Descriptive Subtitles. The screening of Beauty and the Beast on Saturday 7 March is a Family screening. The screening of Beauty and the Beast on Wednesday 18 February will be introduced by Disniversity Podcast’s hosts Ben Travis and Dr Sam Summers.

Behind the Scenes: BFI NETWORK Showcase.description:
The event highlights the work of BFI NETWORK in supporting and sustaining film projects around the UK.

BFI NETWORK collaborates with film organisations and leading cultural venues across the UK to provide short film and early development funding alongside professional development support for early career filmmakers, all thanks to BFI National Lottery funding. Meet the BFI team as they discuss how they work with nurture talent, what it takes to build a support network for producers, writers and directors and their love and passion for short form narrative story telling. Tickets £8.

_additional_info.title: Behind the Scenes: BFI NETWORK Showcase

La Belle et la B\u00eate.description:
1946 — France — Jean Cocteau — 93 min

Cocteau’s take on Beauty and the Beast is a magical, elegant classic.

When Belle’s father becomes beholden to a monstrous beast, she takes his place, staying in the enchanted castle where the beast resides and gradually falling under his spell. It’s difficult to imagine a more magical cinematic experience than Cocteau’s take on the fairy tale. The meticulous production design, the spectacle of the costumes and a fable rich in symbolism and metaphor – it’s a dream you never want to wake from. The screening of La Belle et la Bête on Sunday 22 February is a Family screening. The screening of La Belle et la Bête on Wednesday 11 February will include an introduction. Also available on BFI Player

La Belle et la B\u00eate + intro.description:
1946 — France — Jean Cocteau — 93 min

Also available on BFI Player

Best in Show.description:
2000 — USA — Christopher Guest — 90 min

This partly improvised comic classic follows some of the participants in the prestigious Mayflower Kennel Club Dog Show.

As the Mayflower Kennel Club Dog Show approaches, the competing owners and their dogs prepare to travel to Philadelphia for the opportunity to win the coveted Best in Show award. Christopher Guest and his ensemble of exemplary improvisers turn in beautifully observed mockumentary that is as affectionate as it is hilarious. The screening on Monday 16 February will be presented with Descriptive Subtitles.

The Birds.description:
1963 — USA — Alfred Hitchcock — 119 min — Cert 15

All manner of birds attack the residents of a small Californian community, for no apparent reason, in Hitchcock’s classic suspense thriller.

Hitchcock’s classic thriller, his third adaptation of a Daphne du Maurier tale after Jamaica Inn and Rebecca, sees birds randomly attack the sleepy Californian community of Bodega Bay. From this unusual premise – and most unlikely of antagonists – the filmmaker crafts a masterfully suspenseful tale that is by turns shocking and tense, with special effects that continue to disturb. The screening of The Birds on Wednesday 11 March will be introduced by Professor Lucy Bolton, Queen Mary University of London. See the BFI Reuben Library event New Writings: Acting and Performance in Hitchcock .

Birthrights: Birth of New Talent.description:
A look at the non-fiction that emerged in the later era of multicultural TV through the Birthrights strand.

BBC 1993. Directors Mian Har Ng, Andy Francis. 29min. Digital BBC 1992. Director Gurinder Chadha. 29min. Digital BBC 1991. Directors Ngozi Onwurah, Simon Onwurah. 30min. Digital In the final years of the units, as budgets were reduced and resources were reallocated, multicultural output was more sporadic. Broadcasters sought more high-profile, audience-attracting dramas. Emerging filmmakers were permitted access to the resources of multicultural units, or were commissioned by them. The Birthrights strand featured documentaries by Ngozi Onwurah and Gurinder Chadha, the latter’s playfulness foreshadowing the intergenerational joy of her 1993 feature debut, Bhaji on the Beach.

Black Girl + intro by Ashley Clark.description:
1966 — Senegal-France — Ousmane Sembène — 59 min — Cert 15

The seminal work from the father of African cinema focuses on a domestic worker who emigrates from Senegal to France in hope of a better life.

This haunting, crisply-shot character study follows a hopeful young Senegalese woman who leaves Dakar to work for a bourgeois white family in France. Considered the first feature film made in sub-Saharan Africa by a Black African director, Black Girl confirmed the arrival of a vital cinematic voice and provided a sharp commentary on the pernicious inequalities of the postcolonial order. UK 1966. Director Lionel Ngakane. With Nicolette Robinson, Patrick Hatfield, Thomas Baptiste. 29min. Digital. PG A key figure in the development of pan-African filmmaking, South African-born Lionel Ngakane directed this sprightly drama about the guileless friendship between a Black girl and a white boy, set against the social tensions of 1960s West London.

Black Queer Lives in the Archive.description:
Jason Okundaye discusses queer-focused media in the multicultural corpus.

In May 2024, journalist Jason Okundaye wrote a piece in The Guardian describing the challenges he faced in finding an episode of The Black Bag, discussing the difficulty and challenges of retaining Black archival spaces, and of accessing heritage media. In this screening and Q&A, Jason joins us to explore Black, queer-focusing media of the Multicultural TV era, its impact, and the afterlives of this heritage.

_additional_info.title: Black Queer Lives in the Archive

Blue Steel.description:
1990 — USA — Kathryn Bigelow — 102 min — Cert 18

Jamie Lee Curtis’s rookie police officer is tormented by Ron Silver’s Wall Street psychopath in Kathryn Bigelow’s cat and mouse thriller.

When rookie cop Megan Turner fatally shoots a suspect in a supermarket robbery, she triggers an obsessive game of cat and mouse with a witness-turned-obsessive. Here, Bigelow transitioned into bigger-budget studio filmmaking and broke new ground with the police-procedural genre. Probing the complexities of institutionalised misogyny and violence as a form of intimacy, Bigelow transports audiences on a non-stop thrill ride. Contains scenes of sexual violence and police brutality.

TV Preview: Bridgerton part two (season.description:
2025 — Netflix — Tom Verica — 60 min

Revel in the romance, scandal and goings-on, in what has become one of the most-watched and obsessed-over period dramas of recent years.

From Shondaland and Jess Brownell, Bridgerton returns for a fairytale-inspired fourth season. Bohemian second son Benedict Bridgerton refuses to settle down, despite pleas to the contrary from matriarch Lady Violet Bridgerton. That is until, at Violet’s masquerade ball, Benedict is awestruck by a masked, mysterious Lady in Silver. Join us to witness the story of Benedict and Sophie unfolding and more thrilling regency-era romance as Bridgerton returns for part two of season four. Tickets £17, concessions £14 (Members pay £2.50 less).

A Brief Affair + intro and Q&A.description:
2025 — Italy — Ludovica Rampoldi — 98 min

In Ludovica Rampoldi’s suspenseful psychological thriller, two couples find their lives inextricably – and dangerously – entwined.

Ludovica Rampoldi, one of Italy’s finest screenwriters, here makes her impressive debut as a feature film director. A sophisticated, suspenseful and unsurprisingly well written drama, it homes in on two couples whose lives are unexpectedly entwined. Incorporating themes of adultery, betrayal and revenge, A Brief Affair is an intoxicating entertainment that packs a powerful punch.

Bringing Up Baby.description:
1938 — USA — Howard Hawks — 103 min

A tame leopard brings together a repressed palaeontologist and a fast-talking heiress in Howard Hawks’s comedy classic.

Hepburn and Grant are perfect foils in this role-reversal comedy (Hepburn is the pursuer and Grant the pursued) set in a world where any notion of normality has been suspended. A masterclass in screwball comedy and pitch-perfect timing, Hawks’ non-stop gag-fest builds and sustains sequences of pure anarchy populated by rapid-fire dialogue and, of course, the titular leopard.

Candyman.description:
2021 — USA — Nia DaCosta — 91 min — Cert 15

Nia DaCosta’s reboot of the landmark horror film is no simple remake, but a terrifying reimagining of the story to reflect modern times.

At Chicago’s Cabrini-Green housing projects, the urban myth surrounding the terrible Candyman continues to thrive. It provides local artist Anthony McCoy with inspiration for a new work, which offers a gateway for the demon to re-enter the world and continue his killing spree. The most recent entry in this horror series is sharp and thrilling, balancing genre expectations with social commentary. Not for the faint hearted. The screening of Candyman on Wednesday 18 March will be introduced by Gabriel Leavey, film curator, presenter and BFI Studio Coordinator.

Candyman + intro by Gabriel Leavey, film.description:
2021 — USA — Nia DaCosta — 91 min — Cert 15

Cat People.description:
1942 — USA — Jacques Tourneur — 73 min

This classic RKO horror explores the world of a woman who believes she is descended from a tribe of cat people.

Simone Simon plays Irene, a Serbian woman living in New York, who believes that she is descended from a tribe of cat people who can shape shift into a panther when aroused. It may explain the series of strange events happening around her. Produced by Val Lewton as part of his horror B-movie deal at RKO, Cat People is an elegant supernatural picture with elements of sexual vulnerability and danger.

The Chronology of Water.description:
2025 — USA — Kristen Stewart — 128 min — Cert 18

A woman battles addiction and the scars of abuse in Kristen Stewart’s directorial debut.

Kristen Stewart’s adaptation of Lidia Yuknavitch’s memoir is raw, devastating cinematic poetry, supercharged by Imogen Poots’ tremendous, committed performance. Lidia grows up in a dysfunctional home, with a sexually abusive father. She has passion for swimming – an activity that brings her freedom and control. Her talent for the sport promises her an escape through a college scholarship. However, when she leaves home, she remains haunted by her past. Stewart skilfully channels the visceral spirit of Yuknavitch’s book, creatively experimenting with form and sound to explore how Lidia internalises violence. Her trauma and self-discovery is traced through fragmented memories and stream-of-consciousness vignettes, caught on grainy 16mm film with layered sounds and intimate narration. Like a bracing swim, The Chronology of Water is challenging and intense, but it will leave you feeling invigorated and glad you took the dip. Kimberley Sheehan, Lead Programmer Contains flashing images and scenes of sexual violence. Audio Description available at all screenings. The screenings on Friday 6 February 20:30 NFT3; Saturday 7 February 12:00 NFT2; Sunday 8 February 12:20 NFT3; Tuesday 10 February 14:30 NFT2; Thursday 12 February 20:30 NFT3; Sunday 15 February 15:00 NFT3; Tuesday 17 February 17:50 NFT2 will be presented with Descriptive Subtitles. See a Relaxed screening of The Chronology of Water with Descriptive subtitles (standard ticket price) Wednesday 11 February 18:00 NFT4.

Collective Monologue + director Jessica.description:
2024 — UK-Argentina — Jessica Sarah Rinland — 104 min

We mark the UK launch of Jessica Sarah Rinland’s intimate new film about Argentinian zoos and animal sanctuaries.

Shot in Rinland’s signature attentive style, Collective Monologue documents and explores the circumstances in which animals are cared for across a series of Argentinian zoos and animal rescue centres. Simultaneously moving and thought provoking, Rinland’s film illustrates the complex power of human, animal relations as variously parrots, turtles, anteaters and monkeys receive close, individual care against a backdrop of institutional management and change.

The Conductor + intro by film critic and.description:
1980 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 106 min

John Gielgud’s renowned conductor returns to Poland, which complicates the life of a married couple and their local orchestra.

An internationally renowned conductor of Polish descent (played with gusto by Gielgud) returns to his family’s homeland to conduct a provincial orchestra after meeting the orchestra’s violist – the daughter of an old love. Beloved by Ingmar Bergman, The Conductor comments on the moral decay and stagnation of a society and its artists. It’s a beautifully performed, sensitively directed drama. See other screenings of The Conductor .

The Conductor.description:
1980 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 106 min

John Gielgud’s renowned conductor returns to Poland, which complicates the life of a married couple and their local orchestra.

Constructed, Told, Spoken Season Introdu.description:
This introductory discussion looks at the themes, issues and events featured in this season.

We look at Multicultural television as a movement through the figures that brought many of the programmes to the screen. In discussions with the creators, correspondents and researchers we examine the legacy and reappraise the impact of an underexamined aspect of British Television history. Tickets £6.50.

The Cow.description:
1969 — Iran — Dariush Mehrjui — 105 min

Inspired by Au Hasard Balthazar and Los Olvidados, Dariush Mehrjui’s film transformed Iranian cinema and defined the Iranian New Wave.

A poor farmer in a rural village loves his cow more than anything. When he loses it, his mind gradually descends into folly, triggering a transformation in him. Mehrjui was forced to whitewash the village before shooting, but that wasn’t enough to prevent a ban, for exposing the poverty and primitiveness of rural Iran. Despite this, the film’s international festival success brought recognition for Iranian cinema. Giulia Saccogna Contains scenes of animal cruelty. Restored in 2014 with the participation and cooperation of the Iranian Cinema Organization, with funding by the National Film Archive of Iran and the Pishgamane Cinemaye Aria Laboratory.

Daniel Farson + intro by Matthew Sweet.description:
To celebrate a new BFI release, we follow wunderkind reporter Daniel Farson as he examines Witchcraft, strippers, witches, UFOs and pop stars.

The second BFI Blu-ray and DVD release from the Associated Rediffusion archive features the groundbreaking work of ITV reporter and presenter Daniel Farson. Farson, alongside fellow iconoclast Robin Day at ITN, brought a new breed of British journalism to television in the 1950s and 60s, interrogating traditional beliefs and challenging figures both inside and outside the establishment. This special screening shows Farson at work, crossing swords with various figures, from striptease artists, witches and pop stars to acclaimed writers and figures from the financial world. Daniel Farson’s Guide to Britain: Volume 1 is available on dual format (BFI Blu-ray and DVD) from 16 February.

Detroit.description:
2017 — USA — Kathryn Bigelow — 143 min — Cert 15

Kathryn Bigelow restages the events that took place during the 1967 Detroit riot.

The 1967 Detroit riot was a large-scale civil unrest triggered by racism, economic inequality and police brutality. They were initiated by police raiding a late-night bar with deadly force. Seen from the perspective of characters on both sides, Bigelow and writer Mark Boal (who previously worked with Bigelow on her previous two films) consulted with survivors to capture the emotional truth of what took place. Detroit is a riveting, all-too-timely portrait of a society on the cusp of collapse. Contains scenes of racist violence. Audio Description available at all screenings. The screening on Monday 16 March will be presented with Descriptive Subtitles. Also available on BFI Player

Doctor Who Special Edition: Warriors of.description:
Pennant Roberts

We welcome this preview of another classic re-release from the Doctor Who series.

The Doctor, Tegan and Turlough find themselves at an underwater base on Earth in 2084. Rival superpowers, along with the Silurians and Sea Devils – the original rulers of the planet – are locked in a struggle to control a stock of deadly nuclear weapons. The Fifth Doctor’s final season brings together fan-favourite monsters from the era of his third incarnation, revived in the recent Doctor Who spin-off, The War Between the Land and the Sea. Peter Davison and Janet Fielding will take part in a paid signing following the event. Tickets £17, concessions £14 (Members pay £2.50 less). Doctor Who: The Collection – Season 21 will soon be released on Blu-ray by BBC Studios.

_additional_info.title: Doctor Who Special Edition: Warriors of the Deep

Library Event: Documenting Presence Thro.description:
A discussion about the representation of women activists and how a new perspective can change the way we look at it.

When the voices of women activists are silenced how might their dissent be heard? Referencing her film Crossing Lines and Braiding Voices (2026), Dr Patricia Francis discusses her offer of an alternative filmic language by abandoning semiotic codes and signifiers. This approach has given volume to the two disparate groups of activists featured in her film: women involved in the 1984-1985 miners’ strike, and those involved in the 2016 Black Lives Matter events. Tickets £6.50.

_additional_info.title: Documenting Presence Through Silence: Re-imagining, Re-constructing and Re-presenting Activist Women’s Voices

Elisa + intro and Q&A.description:
2025 — Italy-Switzerland — Leonardo Di Costanzo — 105 min

A powerful prison drama about a convicted murderer finally confronting her crime.

Part-psychological thriller, part-prison drama, Leonardo Di Costanzo’s realistic, sensitively directed story explores the life of Elisa, a prisoner convicted of her sister’s murder. Through encounters with a skilled criminal psychologist, she is gradually forced to confront the reality of her family’s past and, ultimately, her own violent actions.

Everything for Sale.description:
1969 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 99 min

This homage to Wajda’s beloved actor, Zbigniew Cybulski, is a blistering view of the film industry and recalls Fellini’s 8½.

When a leading actor disappears from a film set, his family and crew search for him before tragic news reaches them. Wajda’s homage to his beloved actor Zbigniew Cybulski, the star of Ashes and Diamonds, is also a scathing portrait of the film industry. Weaving together autobiography and fiction, Wajda questions what it means to be an artist, and how we mourn, create legends and remember the past. Contains themes of suicide. Poland 1962. Director Andrzej Wajda. 25min. Digital (restoration). With English subtitles Wajda’s last collaboration with Zbigniew Cybulski grapples with intergenerational misalignment.

Tribute to Claudia Cardinale: The Facts.description:
1959 — Italy — Pietro Germi — 115 min — Cert 15

The great Claudia Cardinale stars in this classic restored Italian crime thriller about two crimes that unfold in the same Rome apartment.

Adapted from Carlo Emilio Gadda’s masterpiece That Awful Mess on the Via Merulana, this is a classic detective thriller about the investigation of two crimes committed in the same Rome apartment building. Showing here in a stunning digital restoration, it is the perfect tribute to the late, great Claudia Cardinale. 4K restoration by L’Immagine Ritrovata at Cineteca di Bologna.

Member Picks: Far from the Madding Crowd.description:
1967 — UK — John Schlesinger — 165 min

Thomas Hardy’s classic novel set in the Victorian West Country provides the basis for this beautifully crafted period drama from John Schlesinger.

Bathsheba Everdene risks the unkind glare of local farming folk when she inherits her uncle’s farm and decides to run it herself. The attentions of several men prove to make life even more complicated, but her outgoing, assured personality provides her with a strong survival instinct. We celebrate John Schlesinger’s centenary with his adaptation – written by Frederick Raphael – of Thomas Hardy’s classic novel. It features a stellar cast and Nic Roeg’s dramatic, colourful cinematography. ‘A compelling examination of a woman navigating the constructive and destructive consequences of love, all framed against the beauty of an English countryside freighted with yearning and pathos.’ – Adam P, BFI Member For a chance to see one of your favourite films on the big screen, share your choice with us, and the reason you love it, at bfi.org.uk/memberpicks . All Member exclusive tickets are just £8 unless otherwise stated. Patrons and Members can book as soon as their priority booking opens and tickets will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. Remaining tickets will be released to the public, as a taster of the benefits of Membership, once public booking opens. Also available on BFI Player

A Fish Called Wanda + intro by Josh Glen.description:
1988 — UK — Charles Crichton — 108 min — Cert 15

Pythons Cleese and Palin join forces with Jamie Lee Curtis and Kevin Kline to create a hilarious, multi-award-winning British comedy.

A hunt for stolen diamonds brings Cleese’s strait-laced English barrister into the sights of Curtis and Oscar-winner Kline’s criminal duo from the US. Ealing comedy legend Charles Crichton spent years working on this critically acclaimed and hugely successful comedy with Cleese, creating a fast-paced and hilarious heist movie that is, quite simply, Wanda-ful. See other screenings of A Fish Called Wanda .

A Fish Called Wanda.description:
1988 — UK — Charles Crichton — 108 min — Cert 15

Pythons Cleese and Palin join forces with Jamie Lee Curtis and Kevin Kline to create a hilarious, multi-award-winning British comedy.

A hunt for stolen diamonds brings Cleese’s strait-laced English barrister into the sights of Curtis and Oscar-winner Kline’s criminal duo from the US. Ealing comedy legend Charles Crichton spent years working on this critically acclaimed and hugely successful comedy with Cleese, creating a fast-paced and hilarious heist movie that is, quite simply, Wanda-ful. The screening of A Fish Called Wanda on Wednesday 4 February will be introduced by Josh Glenn, BFI Production Coordinator.

A Focus on Skin + intro by season curato.description:
Skin’s documentary output chronicles some of the most important junctures of Black and Asian British life.

LWT 1980. Director Jon Guilbert. 27min. Digital LWT 1981. Director Jon Guilbert. 28min. Digital LWT 1981. Directors Trevor Hampton, David W. Rolfe. 25min. Digital LWT 1981. Director John Morgan. 24min. Digital Black Britain appeared to exist as a parallel country. The things that many took for granted, such as schooling, protection and fair housing, were weaponised by the state and required constant community monitoring. Skin was a pioneer in multicultural non-fiction programming, which covered Black Britain across areas as diverse as education, state malfeasance, resistance to far-right group and immigration. The series pushed against engineered media narratives of the early 1980s, documenting uprisings and community resistance to right-wing terror campaigns, including searing coverage of what became known as the ‘New Cross massacre’.

A Focus on the Bandung File + intro by f.description:
The Bandung File was perhaps the most famous show to emerge from the multicultural movement. We look at some of its highlights.

Channel 4 1986. Director Christopher Spencer. 36min. Digital Channel 4 1985. Director David Cohen. 27min. Digital Channel 4 1987. Director Christopher Spencer. 38min. Digital UK 1988. Director Christopher Spencer. 52min. Digital Bandung File drew on the political reporting of Race Today, which inspired mass action with a global non-aligned perspective, but replacing the magazine format with incisive reporting that spotlighted injustice across the globe. Too Many Questions focuses on racist border policing. Smile Jamaica and a profile of Haiti are detailed analyses captured in the aftermath of disasters. A later programme looks back at the Grunwick Strike.

_additional_info.title: A Focus on the Bandung File

Fuori + intro and Q&A.description:
2025 — Italy-France — Mario Martone — 117 min

Valeria Golino is outstanding in Mario Martone’s bravura biopic about legendary Art of Joy novelist Goliarda Sapienza.

Skilfully directed by Mario Martone, Fuori is an utterly convincing, raw and moving portrait of the brilliant and complex writer Goliarda Sapienza. Set during the 1980s, when Sapienza was largely unrecognised, the film is anchored by powerhouse performance by Golino, who previously directed the recent, acclaimed television adaptation of Sapienza’s own Art of Joy.

Galentine\u2019s Day: But I\u2019m a Che.description:
1999 — USA — Jamie Babbit — 92 min — Cert 15

Serve camp 1990s realness with your pals this Galentine’s Day, with Jamie Babbit’s cult classic of queer cinema.

All-American teen Megan has a jock boyfriend and place on the cheerleading squad. But it’s not enough to stop her parents suspecting she’s a lesbian. Sent to True Directions conversion therapy camp, Megan is confronted with her actual identity, with far more queer results than her parents hoped for. Dubbed the ‘gay Clueless’ by director Jamie Babbit, this tongue-in-cheek cult classic sees an iconic cast hilariously tackle themes of gender and sexuality. Contains homophobic attitudes and language. Tickets £17 concessions £14 (members pay £2.50 less). Woman with a Movie Camera is generously supported by Jane Stanton.

_additional_info.title: Galentine’s Day: But I’m a Cheerleader

Gamera vs. Barugon.description:
1966 — Japan — Shigeo Tanaka — 101 min

An epic battle between heavyweight monsters brings about chaos and destruction.

Gamera returns to battle giant lizard Barugon, which recently hatched and is causing havoc. A powerful beast, it possesses a deadly rainbow ray which threatens humanity’s very existence. Japan’s military have used all their might to stop the beast, but the only hope now lies with Gamera, which takes the battle to Barugon across a variety of locations around the country.

Gamera vs. Gyaos.description:
1967 — Japan — Noriaki Yuasa — 87 min

The unbeatable Gamera meets its match in a further monster mash-up.

The Japanese people look to the skies for the latest blight on the country’s population. The giant winged monster Gyaos seems intent on destroying the world and, once again, it seems only Gamera can save the day. These films were not widely seen in the UK and the international premiere of these splendid digital 4K restorations closes with this classic of the genre.

Gamera.description:
1965 — Japan — Noriaki Yuasa — 79 min

The military is on red alert when a giant turtle attacks in this newly restored monster movie.

The huge success of the Godzilla movies paved the way for many other films that captured global apprehension over the Atomic Age, including the fantastic series of films featuring giant, fire-breathing turtle monster Gamera. This first instalment, a classic origins story, was so popular it spawned a number of sequels and is a fine example of this genre at the very pinnacle of its popularity.

UK Premiere of 4K Restoration: The Garde.description:
1928 — USA — Lewis Milestone — 80 min

Delightfully saucy, The Garden of Eden is arguably Lewis Milestone’s most successful romantic comedy.

Minus only the gatling-gun dialogue, this is effectively a silent screwball. Scripted by Hans Kraly, Lubitsch’s regular writer, the film follows the fortunes of Corinne Griffith’s radiant young singer as she flees a pretzel bakery for the bright lights of Budapest, only to find herself on offer to wealthy men in a disreputable music hall. The action then traces her journey to Monte Carlo and the notorious Hotel Eden, where Viennese comedy joyfully turns to French farce. Restored in 4K in 2025 by San Francisco Film Preserve. In collaboration with George Eastman Museum, Library of Congress and The Maltese Film Works. Funding provided by Sunrise Foundation for Education and the Arts.

_additional_info.title: UK Premiere of 4K Restoration: The Garden of Eden

Gioia + intro and Q&A.description:
2025 — Italy — Nicolangelo Gelormini — 108 min

Valeria Golino and Saul Nanni are mesmerising in this enthralling drama about an introverted teacher and her dangerously manipulative pupil.

Gelormini follows his excellent debut feature, Fortuna: The Girl and the Giants, with this enthralling noir, adapted from a theatre piece. Golino plays Gioia, a bookish schoolteacher, who is drawn out of her mundane existence by the seductive yet fraudulent attentions of Alessio, a criminally unscrupulous pupil.

Library Event: Graveyard Shift.description:
Join us to seek out missing information to enhance the BFI’s ever-growing database.

Calling all cinephile sleuths! Join us in the BFI Reuben Library for the Graveyard Shift – a public research event to find death dates of people involved in key filmmaking roles to enhance the BFI’s data and knowledge of copyright in our collections. Utilising a range of resources, participants will work in teams to compete against each other – and the clock – to improve these unique records of filmmaking history. With the support of the BFI Screen Heritage Fund, awarding National Lottery funding.

Grizzly Man.description:
2005 — USA — Werner Herzog — 104 min — Cert 15

Werner Herzog’s powerful documentary about grizzly bear obsessive Timothy Treadwell also reveals much about the filmmaker’s own view of nature.

Werner Herzog turns his camera on the passionate, fearless and extraordinarily eccentric Timothy Treadwell, who dedicated a good portion of his life living close to brown bears in one of Alaska’s national parks. Herzog corrals hours of footage shot be Treadwell to chronicle his life in the wild, his enthusiasm for the bears and the risks he took, which eventually ended in tragedy. Widely acknowledged as one of the best documentaries of the last 20 years, Grizzly Man is both a cautionary tale and a fascinating contemplation of our relationship with nature.

Hard Boiled.description:
1992 — Hong Kong — John Woo — 128 min — Cert 18

Police and gangsters collide in John Woo’s explosive shoot ‘em-ups – one of the coolest action films ever made.

John Woo’s police-action masterpiece about a vengeful cop taking down an weapons-smuggling syndicate looks sensational newly restored in 4K. In a Hong Kong teahouse, police inspector ‘Tequila’ Yuen heads a team surveiling a group of weapons-smugglers that is about to make deal. The operation goes badly wrong when a rival gang arrives and a fierce shootout breaks out. Tequila’s partner is killed, sending him spiralling with rage and vengeance on quest to hunt down the gang. Woo’s explosive film is a landmark of ‘heroic bloodshed’, a stylistic movement of 80s and 90s Hong Kong action cinema that fused visual flare with melodramatic themes of brotherhood and honour. The filmmaker’s signature style is in full force here: elegant, swirling, slow-motion camera work captures intricately choreographed fistfights and shootouts. Quite simply, action has rarely looked this good. Kimberley Sheehan, Lead Programmer Contains scenes of graphic violence.

Harvey.description:
1950 — USA — Henry Koster — 104 min

James Stewart shines in this tale of an eccentric, mild-mannered man whose closest friend is an invisible six-foot rabbit.

Elwood P. Dowd is an eccentric whose best friend is an invisible 6-foot-tall rabbit named Harvey. Elwood’s family are outcasts within their community, so they decide to seek professional help for him. But are their concerns for Elwood founded, or does Harvey actually exist? Adapted from Mary Coyle Chase’s Pulitzer Prize-winning stage play, Harvey features James Stewart at his homespun best, firing on all cylinders as the loveable Elwood.

Heads or Tails? + intro and Q&A.description:
2025 — Italy-USA — Alessio Rigo de Righi, Matteo Zoppis — 116 min

A surreal, frequently hilarious take on the spaghetti western, about a couple on the run.

Rodeo riders, ghosts, political rebels and Reilly’s Buffalo Bill all feature in this weird, wild and wacky Spaghetti Western. Channelling the influence of Sergio Leone and Sergio Corbucci – masters of the European Western – Righi and Zoppis also tip their hats to Robert Altman’s 1970s revisionist take on the genre, McCabe and Mrs Miller, delivering a hugely enjoyable, picaresque and blacky comic proto-feminist horse opera.

Homebound + journalist Nabanita Sircar i.description:
2025 — India — Neeraj Ghaywan — 122 min

Two childhood friends chase the same dream in Neeraj Ghaywan’s moving drama, which was executive produced by Martin Scorsese.

Friends since childhood, Dalit Chandan and Muslim Shoaib are both determined to join the police; they believe that a uniform will provide them with the dignity they seek. However, competition for the job is intense and the challenges they face along the way threaten to undermine their friendship. Neeraj Ghaywan’s (Masaan) second feature is a beautifully crafted drama that explores friendship and resilience, as well as the challenges of caste and religious identity.

A House of Dynamite.description:
2025 — USA — Kathryn Bigelow — 112 min — Cert 15

Kathryn Bigelow thrillingly dissects a US government’s response to a nuclear attack of unknown origin.

When a single, unattributed missile is launched at the US, a race begins to determine who is responsible and how to respond. Bigelow’s thriller presents a gripping, visceral and unsettlingly credible scenario, seen from three perspectives across the same, short time-span. With an all-star ensemble cast, Bigelow focuses in on the individuals responsible for critical global security systems, whose humanity conflicts with the pressures of their roles. Once again, it highlights Bigelow’s skill as one of contemporary cinema’s most kinetic, compelling and precise filmmakers. Audio Description available at all screenings. The screening on Thursday 5 March will be presented with Descriptive Subtitles. Closed Captions available via WatchWord smart glasses – please see our Closed Captions page for a list of screenings.

TV Preview: How to Get to Heaven from Be.description:
Michael Lennox

From the writer and creator of Derry Girls, Lisa McGee, comes the new series How to Get to Heaven from Belfast.

The new drama by Lisa McGee, the creator of Derry Girls, focuses on chaotic TV writer Saoirse, stressed-out mother of three Robyn and dependable carer Dara. They grew up together in a quiet northern Ireland town and have remained a tight-knit group. When an email informs them about the death of the estranged fourth member of their childhood gang, they decide to go to her wake. But a series of eerie events take place as they travel across Ireland and a dark childhood secret appears threatens to be revealed. Tickets £17, concessions £14 (Members pay £2.50 less).

_additional_info.title: How to Get to Heaven from Belfast

Hunting Flies.description:
1969 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 109 min

This is a rare chance to see Andrzej Wajda working in a comedic mode, to impressive effect.

An outlier in Wajda’s body of work, his only comedy feature focuses on bookshop worker Włodek’s encounter with the strong and independent Irena, whose ambitions to turn him into a successful writer go wildly awry. A fascinating attempt by Wajda at working in a different mode in order to explore the crisis of masculinity, it features a standout performance by Braunek. Poland 1968. Director Andrzej Wajda. 35min. Digital. With English subtitles This sci-fi comedy is an adaptation of Stanisław Lem’s work about a racing car driver whose multiple organ transplants find him acquiring the donors’ personalities.

The Hurt Locker.description:
2008 — USA — Kathryn Bigelow — 131 min — Cert 15

Kathryn Bigelow’s Oscar-winning film follows an elite bomb disposal team during the Iraq conflict.

Jeremy Renner plays Sergeant First Class William James, a loose-cannon explosive ordnance disposal expert, whose unorthodox approach to his job in the second Iraq War unsettles his colleagues. Bigelow made history as the first woman to win the Academy Award for Best Director with this tense, but insightful, portrait of soldiers addicted to adrenaline and duty. Handheld close-ups combine with precise framing to deliver a visceral and immersive exploration of the chaos, horror and psychological toll of war. Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

Innocent Sorcerers.description:
1960 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 87 min

This French New Wave-esque, jazz-fuelled drama is an account of one night in the life of a man and a woman.

Immediately following his lauded war trilogy, Wajda turned his camera on Poland’s socially modern but politically disengaged post-war generation. When hipster doctor Bazyli meets out-of-towner Pelagia in a nightclub, they spend a night in his flat flirting to the jazz tunes of Krzysztof Komeda. Embracing a style similar to the contemporaneous French New Wave, this is a vivid portrait of disillusioned youth. Poland 1951. Director Andrzej Wajda. 6min. Digital (restoration). With English subtitles A boy spies on a kissing couple, which triggers serious consequences for the pair.

Jaws.description:
1975 — USA — Steven Spielberg — 124 min

Steven Spielberg’s groundbreaking classic, one of the first modern blockbusters, is a masterclass in terror and suspense.

There’s a great white shark off the coastline of tourist destination Amity Island as it heads into Independence Day, yet the local mayor and his minions seem unwilling to take the threat seriously. But following another attack, the town’s sheriff, an oceanographer and an expert shark hunter set off to kill the beast. Spielberg’s film redefined the cinema blockbuster making the most of John William’s suspenseful score and a mechanical shark the film’s crew named ‘Bruce’. The screening on Monday 16 March will be presented with Descriptive Subtitles.

K-19: The Widowmaker.description:
2002 — USA — Kathryn Bigelow — 138 min

Harrison Ford and Liam Neeson lead Kathryn Bigelow’s tense nuclear submarine thriller.

In the early 1960s, the Soviet Union’s first nuclear-powered ballistic submarine journeys into the Arctic to test its missile launching capabilities. During the mission, the crew discover the vessel’s nuclear reactor is leaking, putting their lives at risk and threatening to destabilise the geopolitical balance. Bigelow’s tense submarine drama turns survival into a ticking clock, exploring her interest in human nature under pressure, when duty and danger collide in one of the world’s most inhospitable environments.

The War Trilogy: Kanal + pre-recorded in.description:
1957 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 96 min

A harrowing portrait of resistance fighters forced to flee the German army via Warsaw’s sewage system remains one of Wajda’s finest achievements.

A unit of Polish freedom fighters goes underground to escape German troops, in the final stages of the 1944 Warsaw Uprising. Wajda’s claustrophobic, nightmarish masterpiece employs haunting images to convey their struggle as they journey through the city’s sewers. The film that brought international acclaim for the director, Kanal is based on true events. It is an evocative portrait of the Polish resistance movement and a heartbreaking depiction of strength, duty and hope in the face of insurmountable odds. Joint ticket available with the screenings of A Generation and Ashes and Diamonds on Sunday 15 February. Tickets £28.50, concessions £22.50 (Members pay £3 less). Book in person at the box office or by phone on 020 7928 3232. See other screenings of Kanal . Also available on BFI Player

The screening of Kanal on Sunday 15 February will include a pre-recorded intro by Professor Annette Insdorf, Columbia University. Also available on BFI Player

Katyn + intro by film critic Carmen Gray.description:
2007 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 122 min — Cert 15

A deeply personal film for Andrzej Wajda, presenting an account of the 1940 Katyn massacre and its aftermath.

Wajda focuses on personal stories and a wider human tragedy in this Oscar-nominated film, set against one of the most painful and politically sensitive topics in Polish history: the 1940 massacre of thousands of Polish soldiers and intellectuals in the Katyn forest. A personal project for Wajda, whose father was murdered in the massacre, Katyn poignantly frames historical events through the stories of women looking for the truth about their missing relatives. See other screenings of Katyn .

Katyn.description:

A deeply personal film for Andrzej Wajda, presenting an account of the 1940 Katyn massacre and its aftermath.

Mark Kermode Live in 3D at the BFI (Febr.description:
The critic presents the latest episode of his live discussion, on stage in NFT1.

A monthly conversation between you, the audience, and one of the nation’s favourite and most respected film critics. Joined by surprise guests from across the film industry, Kermode explores, critiques and dissects current and upcoming releases, cinematic treasures, industry news and even some guilty pleasures. Get involved @KermodeMovie #MK3D. Tickets £22, concessions £19 (Members pay £2.50 less).

_additional_info.title: Mark Kermode Live in 3D at the BFI

Kes.description:
1969 — UK — Ken Loach — 111 min

This authentic look at growing up in a 60s mining town is joyful, challenging and a British classic.

Young Billy lives in a South Yorkshire mining community and is treated as harshly at home as he is at school. But his life changes dramatically when he takes charge of a young kestrel. His growing interest in falconry is a pursuit that gives him a sense of being and helps shield him from the bleakness of daily life. Loach’s breakthrough film, which remains one of his finest, is an uncompromising portrait of youth whose harshness is balanced with moments of humour. The screening of Kes on Tuesday 17 March is a Family screening.

Killer of Sheep.description:
1978 — USA — Charles Burnett — 80 min — Cert 15

Charles Burnett’s multifaceted portrait of community life in Los Angeles is one of the great US directorial debuts.

Burnett’s feature debut went mostly unseen for decades. Part of a breakout LA movement in American independent cinema, it’s a beautifully meditative set of vignettes creates a kaleidoscope of Black working-class life in Los Angeles’ Watts district. Xavier Alexandre Pillai Contains scenes of animal cruelty and racist language. Digitally restored to 4K and remastered by UCLA Film & Television Archive, Milestone Films, and the Criterion Collection. Restoration supervised by Ross Lipman and Jillian Borders in consultation with Charles Burnett.

Korczak + Q&A.description:
1990 — Poland-Germany-UK — Andrzej Wajda — 118 min

A heartbreaking portrait of Janusz Korczak, a Polish-Jewish educator and paediatrician, during the Second World War.

An account of the last years of Janusz Korczak, the heroic Polish Jewish educator and paediatrician, saw Wajda collaborate on the screenplay with Agnieszka Holland. The topic of Jewishness within Polish history and society is a feature of a number of Wajda’s films. Korczak is arguably his most resonant, and vital, account of the Holocaust, while also exploring themes of self-sacrifice, honour and the strength of the human spirit, even in the face of evil. See other screenings of Korczak .

Korczak.description:
1990 — Poland-Germany-UK — Andrzej Wajda — 118 min

A heartbreaking portrait of Janusz Korczak, a Polish-Jewish educator and paediatrician, during the Second World War.

The screening of Korczak on Monday 2 March will include a Q&A.

MilkTea presents \u2013 UK Premiere: Las.description:
2025 — USA — Justin Lin — 120 min

A fascinating portrait of a young missionary whose desire to spread the gospel resulted in tragedy.

Justin Lin’s (Star Trek Beyond, Fast X) return to independent cinema details the tragic events surrounding modern-day Christian missionary John Allen Chau’s attempt to convert the inhabitants of the remote North Sentinel Island, who have had no contact with the outside world. The film premiered to acclaim at the Sundance Film Festival and stars impressive newcomer Sky Yang, who was discovered by Lin three years ago at a MilkTea event here at BFI Southbank.

_additional_info.title: MilkTea presents – UK Premiere: Last Days

The Last One for the Road + intro and Q&.description:
2025 — Italy-Germany — Francesco Sossai — 100 min

Francesco Sossai’s smart satire details a road trip taken around the Veneto countryside by a trio of misfits.

In this idiosyncratic, sardonic and slyly funny tale, two middle-aged misfits ramble by car around the Veneto countryside, picking up a shy architectural student on their wayward travels. With echoes of Don Quixote, this ambling shaggy dog tale is shot through with understated wit and psychological insight. It’s a genuinely distinctive film that offers a refreshing take on contemporary Italian life.

_additional_info.title: The Last One for the Road

Liberation Struggles.description:
Multicultural television traced and covered liberation struggles through the lens of non-aligned politics.

Channel 4 1983. Director Lincoln Browne. 41min. Digital Channel 4 1986. Directors Christopher Spencer, Holly Aylett. 40min. Digital Channel 4 1996. Director Sabiha Sumar. 27min. Digital From the battle for Tamil self-determination in Sri Lanka to Apartheid in South Africa, multicultural programming often stood on the front lines of international issues. These editions give an insight into battles being fought globally. Regular updates from Bandung File ranged from the harrowing impact of Apartheid on the lives of children to politics in Pakistan, while the documentary series Black Bag shone a light on the female members of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam.

The Loveless.description:
1982 — USA — Kathryn Bigelow, Monty Montgomery — 82 min — Cert 15

Willem Dafoe is a biker who attracts trouble in this enjoyable, subversive outlaw drama.

A motorcycle gang of greasers roars into a small southern American town in the 1950s, looking for fun and unsettling the locals. Vance, the gang’s charismatic leader soon hooks up with the troubled daughter of a local businessman, raising the temperature further. Co-directed with Monty Montgomery (who went on to produce David Lynch’s Wild at Heart), former artist Bigelow’s feature debut is a blisteringly raw, angry and lust-charged drama, dominated by a charismatic Willem Dafoe in his big screen debut. Contains scenes of suicide.

The Maids of Wilko + intro.description:
1979 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 118 min

A Chekhovian tale focusing on a man’s return to a village of his youth, where he re-encounters a group of sisters he was once intimate with.

After the death of a close friend, Wiktor returns to a place of his youth. He re-encouragers a group of sisters with whom he spent an idyllic summer 15 years prior, discovering the extent to which their lives have changed. Wajda’s most lyrical and poetic work marked a shift in pace and tone, allowing him to meditate on questions of passing time, regret and unfulfilled love. Contains themes of suicide. See other screenings of The Maids of Wilko .

The Maids of Wilko.description:
1979 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 118 min

A Chekhovian tale focusing on a man’s return to a village of his youth, where he re-encounters a group of sisters he was once intimate with.

After the death of a close friend, Wiktor returns to a place of his youth. The screening of The Maids of Wilko on Thursday 5 February will include an introduction.

Malcolm X + intro by Ashley Clark.description:
1992 — USA — Spike Lee — 201 min — Cert 15

See Spike Lee’s epic film of the life of Malcolm X, screening from a new 35mm print.

Spike Lee’s magnificent biopic of the eponymous activist and orator – embodied by Denzel Washington in an astonishing, Academy Award-nominated performance – combines a vast sweep reminiscent of the great cinematic epics with a propulsive stylistic verve characteristic of Lee at his freewheeling best. Exhilarating, absorbing and deeply moving, Malcolm X is an unforgettable monument to its subject. New 35mm print made with funding from the National Lottery and the additional support of donors to our Keep Film on Film campaign. With thanks to Warner Bros. and YCM Laboratories.

The Solidarity Trilogy: Wa\u0142\u0119sa.description:
2013 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 127 min

A biopic of Lech Wałęsa, one of the most significant political figures in 20th-century Polish history.

The third film in the director’s Solidarity Trilogy, Wajda’s portrait of Lech Wałęsa, leader of Poland’s Solidarity movement, recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize and one of the country’s most significant political figures, is a rousing biopic. It skilfully explores the different facets of Wałęsa, both as a complex national hero and an ordinary family man, while at the same considering what it means to create a national legend and what it takes to persevere in the face of suppression. Joint ticket available with the screenings of Man of Marble and Man of Iron on Sunday 1 March. Tickets £28.50, concessions £22.50 (Members pay £3 less). Book in person at the box office or by phone on 020 7928 3232.

The Solidarity Trilogy: Man of Iron.description:
1981 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 152 min

This Cannes Palme d’Or winner focuses on a Solidarity leader and the journalist investigating him.

The Palme d’Or-winning follow-up to Man of Marble sees Winkel, a Communist-friendly radio journalist, charged with finding compromising information about a Solidarity opposition leader. But in witnessing protesting workers’ fight against political propaganda and commitment to overturn a repressive regime, Winkel questions his own beliefs. Directly addressing the contemporary political situation as Poland entered the 1980s, Man of Iron combines fact and fiction to stunning effect, resulting in one of Wajda’s most profound artistic achievements. Joint ticket available with the screenings of Man of Marble and Man of Hope on Sunday 1 March. Tickets £28.50, concessions £22.50 (Members pay £3 less). Book in person at the box office or by phone on 020 7928 3232.

The Solidarity Trilogy: Man of Marble.description:
1976 — Poland — Andrzej Wajda — 161 min

One of Andrzej Wajda’s landmark films tells the story of a filmmaker searching for the truth about a forgotten workers’ hero.

In the 1970s, young filmmaker Agnieszka investigates the life of a 1950s bricklayer and worker’s hero. When she learns that the facts behind his story were suppressed, she has to decide whether to pursue the truth or not. Man of Marble is a thought-provoking examination of the moral responsibility of an individual and art in challenging dominant ideology, censorship and oppressive authorities. It’s a powerful milestone in Polish cinema. Joint ticket available with the screenings of Man of Iron and Man of Hope on Sunday 1 March. Tickets £28.50, concessions £22.50 (Members pay £3 less). Book in person at the box office or by phone on 020 7928 3232.

Member Exclusive: BFI Southbank and BFI.description:
An exclusive tour for BFI Members.

Members are offered an exclusive tour of our venues. You’ll have the chance to visit the NFT1 projection booth, uncover the secrets stored in the BFI Reuben Library, tour the archive on display at BFI Mediatheque and go behind the scenes of the UK’s largest screen – the BFI IMAX. Tour will run until 13:30. Tickets £8. If you have any access requirements, please contact us at membership@bfi.org.uk .

_additional_info.title: BFI Southbank and BFI IMAX Tour

BFI Member Oscar Quiz.description:
Join our Member quiz and see how much you really know about the film calendar’s glitziest night.

As Hollywood’s biggest night approaches, we will be putting your knowledge to the test with our latest BFI Member Quiz. Join us at the BFI IMAX bar as we delve into almost a century of Oscar history. It will likely feature winners and losers, famous speeches and controversial moments that people still talk about – more than enough to test your knowledge. Come along and see if you can take home top prize! Teams limited to a maximum of four people. Tickets £8.

35th Anniversary Screening: Mississippi.description:
1991 — USA-UK — Mira Nair — 118 min — Cert 15

Mira Nair’s 90s drama carefully balances tender romance with themes of cultural differences, racism and colourism.

Forced to flee their home in Uganda, an Indian family emigrates to Mississippi to run a motel. While her parents grapple with the trauma of displacement, young Mina quickly adapts to American life. After two chance run-ins with Washington’s carpet cleaner Demetrius, she begins to fall deeply in love with him. But the prejudices of their conservative families threaten to upend this blossoming romance. Contains racist attitudes and language.

Multicultural TV in Europe + intro.description:
Europe offered a counterpoint to the UK in race relations. These analyses changed over time to be more focused on personal experiences.

Channel 4 1985. Director Greg Lanning. 27min. Digital BBC 1991. Series Producer Onyekachi Wambu. 30min. Digital UK 2015. Director Cecile Emeke. 11min. Digital France 2018. Director Kader Attia. 48min. Digital Early explorations of multicultural TV looked at Europe, through the lens of interconnected forms of global oppression. Over time, focus on the lived experiences of multi-ethnic people increased. Here we juxtapose documentaries focusing on the lives of racialised communities in France to reveal how conversations, cultures and analyses of lived experience have become foregrounded in non-fiction.

Multicultural TV on the BBC.description:
To rival Channel 4, the BBC established its own multicultural units. We revisit their output.

BBC 1983. Series Producer Keith Sheather. 30min. Digital BBC 1982. Producer Ashok Rampal. 30min. Digital. With English subtitles BBC 1987. Director Waseem Mahmood. 40min. Digital In response to Channel 4’s initiation of Black programming, the BBC started its own multicultural departments, setting up a production unit for African-Caribbean shows in 1982 and subsequently launching Ebony. The BBC’s Asian output also changed as Asian Magazine was modernised and became Network East. In these examples of the series’ programming, Ebony follows young photographer Vanley Burke, while Network East tells the story of a family forced to take shelter in a temple to avoid deportation.

Multicultural TV on Channel 4.description:
When Channel 4 arrived as the new channel it had multicultural programming built into its programming. We look at two of its earliest and biggest shows.

Channel 4 1985. Director Michael Toppin. 54min. Digital Channel 4 1983. Director Trevor Hampton. 55min. Digital A new channel saw the emergence of a new era. Ceaseless campaigning saw Black programming incorporated into the structure of Channel 4. The two flagship shows of the multicultural department, hybrids of variety programming and political reporting, ran until the mid 80s. Eastern Eye focuses on a very different and much-needed kind of British pirate radio station: Asian People’s Radio. Black on Black features the reggae awards and hears from the soon to be queen of Lover’s Rock, Janet Kay.

Multicultural TV on ITV.description:
We review the beginning of ITV’s multicultural output.

LWT 1974. 27min. Digital ATV 1981. Director Terence Daw. 27min. Digital LWT 1980. Director Nic Phillips. 28min. Digital Urban centres bloomed with multicultural plurality. From London to Birmingham, young Black Britons pushed their talents, eventually finding outlets on variety television programmes. Initially, ITV attempted to rival the BBC with community access programming like Speak for Yourself. Eventually, the channel found its own lane as an early pioneer of the multicultural variety format. Variety programming such as Here and Now, was one of the first iterations in the midlands. The episode veers from covering Vitamin D deficiency to young Black musical and sporting talent.

Multiculturalism Goes Mainstream.description:
A look back at the moment the programming began to shift to a more populist approach.

BBC 2001. Director Gurdip Singh Bhangoo. 29min. Digital BBC 2002. Director Sunandan Walia. 29min. Digital BBC 2003. Director Petal Felix. 60min. Digital Multicultural TV gradually became more mainstream. The East episode on beauty standards from 1992 mirrors the tonal shift as glossy gossip reporting thrived in an increasingly commercial media landscape, a decade on the programme follows sitar superstar Anoushka Shankar. In Black Britain journalist Adrian Chiles takes a road trip around the UK, earnestly appraising multiculturalism. It provides a fascinating reflection of the era, which reveals the hopeful but misguided politics of a ‘post-racial’ Britain. The inclusion of the far-right now appears as a harbinger for our current media culture.

My Father\u2019s Shadow.description:
2025 — UK-Nigeria — Akinola Davies Jr — 94 min

Two brothers connect with their father in this drama set against the backdrop of the 1993 Nigerian presidential election.

In Akinola Davies Jr.’s stunning directorial feature debut, two siblings spend a rare day with their mysterious father, who takes them on a trip to Lagos. Young brothers Remi and Akin are playing outside their home in rural Nigeria when their absent father arrives and announces he is taking them to the country’s largest city. As they journey through Lagos, which awaits the results of the 1993 presidential election, they sense an air of heightened uncertainty and witness growing unrest, all the time observing sides of their father they had never previously seen. Davies Jr.’s debut is a wonderfully textured work, alive with detail and simmering with a powerful emotional undertow. Lagos, seen in intimate close up from the children’s perspective, is a vibrant rush of chaos and heat, bringing the boys precious moments with their father. Ṣọpẹ́ Dìrísù (Gangs of London, His House) is exceptional, balancing sternness and tenderness in equal measure. The film was awarded a Special Mention in Caméra d’Or Prize at the Cannes Film Festival and garnered twelve nominations at the British Independent Film Awards, with Davies Jr winning Best Director. Kimberley Sheehan, Lead Programmer Contains scenes of graphic violence. Audio Description available at all screenings.
